sections.overview: Empis opaca is a European dance fly in the family Empididae and genus Empis.
sections.identification: Adults are about six to ten millimetres long, with reddish legs and four dark thoracic stripes that distinguish them from Empis livida.
sections.habitat: It is reported along hedgerows and woodland edges and occurs in cooler parts of Europe.
sections.diet: Adults prey on other insects and also take nectar from flowers.
sections.behavior: Males may present a dead insect as a nuptial gift, which the female eats during mating.
sections.reproduction: Field accounts report that females may reject males without a prey gift; egg and larval biology remain poorly documented in the sources used.
sections.ecology: It is mainly recorded from April to early June, and its spring adults hunt insects and visit flowers.
sections.conservation: NatureSpot describes it as fairly common in England and Wales, with fewer records from Scotland, but this is not a Europe-wide trend assessment.
